A PRU remains in position to pressure Berlin. What are A BER and A BOH doing this spring? I’ll keep A MOS out of German centers if your forces stay clear of Russian centers, but I won’t promise to leave PRU idle.
I propose keeping the southern front quiet this spring: F BLA and A SEV will stay out of the Black Sea and your centers. Will F ANK stay out of the Black Sea, and will A BUL remain out of Rumania?

Turkey to Russia: Spring 1908. Your A RUM, F BLA and A SEV sit on my northern border. I need to know whether A RUM or A SEV moves toward Bulgaria or Constantinople this spring. My A BUL and A CON will hold if your southern units stay out of Bulgaria, Armenia and the Black Sea coast. Answer in writing.

I’ll keep F ENG clear of Belgium and Holland this spring, as proposed, provided F HOL stays out of Denmark and my other centers. F DEN will not move against Holland or Belgium. Please confirm F HOL is not targeting Denmark.

F DEN will stay clear of Sweden and the Baltic, and my other fleets will not target your centers. I’m keeping F NOR clear of Norway; F EDI, F LON, and F ENG will remain focused on protecting my position. A PRU can pressure Germany without conflicting with me.

France to Germany: Spring 1908. I will keep A PAR out of Burgundy, Ruhr and Belgium this spring, and A GAS stays out of Munich and Marseille. My focus remains Spain and Portugal. Please keep A BUR and A MAR out of Picardy, Gascony and Brest, and I will hold my border quiet while we both watch the north.

France to England: Spring 1908. F MAO is moving south toward Portugal, not the Channel, and F BRE stays in Brest this spring. I have no fleet heading into the Channel or North Sea. Keep your fleets off Brest and Picardy as well, and I will do the same with my English-facing units.

A MAR and A PIE will stay out of Piedmont and Tunis this spring. A TYR is no longer in my forces; A MUN will hold and will not move toward Trieste or Venice. Please keep A TUN and F WES clear of Marseille and Burgundy.

A BUR will hold this spring, and no German unit will enter Brest or Picardy. A PIC is no longer in my forces. I’ll keep A MAR out of French territory; please keep A PAR and A GAS clear of Burgundy, Ruhr, and Munich, and stay out of Belgium.

A BER will defend Berlin against A PRU, and A BOH will hold. I’ll keep my forces out of Russian centers if A MOS stays clear of German territory. I can’t accept PRU entering Berlin; please redirect it or leave it in place.

F HOL will support Belgium’s defense, and A BEL will hold there. F HOL will stay out of Denmark and your other centers. Since you’re not proposing a move against Belgium, please keep your fleets clear of Holland and Belgium this spring.

A RUM will stay out of Serbia and Galicia this spring, and A SWE and A PRU will not move toward Warsaw or Galicia. Please keep A BUD and A VIE out of Russian territory; I cannot make broader commitments about future turns.

I’ll keep A MOS out of German centers this spring, but A PRU remains a threat to Berlin and I won’t promise to leave it idle. Keep your units out of Russian centers and avoid escalating elsewhere on the eastern front.
A RUM and A SEV will not move toward Bulgaria or Constantinople this spring; F BLA will stay out of the Black Sea. In return, please keep F ANK out of the Black Sea and A BUL out of Rumania.

A SWE will hold and A NOR will stay clear of your centers. Please keep F DEN clear of Sweden and F NOR clear of Russian centers as proposed. My other forces are focused on the southern and German fronts.

Turkey to Russia: Spring 1908. F ANK stays out of the Black Sea this spring and A BUL will not enter Rumania. In return, I need written confirmation that A RUM does not move to Bulgaria or Constantinople, and A SEV and F BLA stay out of the Black Sea coast and Armenia. If A RUM moves, I will contest it at once.

Austria to Russia: Fall 1908. Your A RUM and A SEV are close to my Balkan border. Will A RUM and A UKR stay out of Galicia and Serbia this fall? I will keep A BUD, A SER and A VIE out of Russian territory. Tell me plainly what A SIL and A FIN do.

Austria to Germany: Fall 1908. Your A SIL and A BOH are near my northern border. Will you confirm A BOH stays out of Vienna and Tyrolia stays away from Trieste this fall? I will keep A VIE and A BUD out of German territory if you do.

Austria to Turkey: Fall 1908. Your A BUL and A GRE have held steadily. I want assurance that A BUL stays out of Serbia and Trieste while we both press Russia. I keep A SER and A BUD out of Bulgaria and Greece. Tell me before any change.

Your F HOL and A BEL remain the obstacle to my position. Are you willing to withdraw F HOL to KIE and keep A BEL defensive this autumn? If not, I may have to contest Holland. What are your plans for F HOL and A BEL?

Can we coordinate pressure on Germany this autumn? I can threaten Holland from the North Sea; please tell me whether A SIL or A WAR will move against German positions. I’ll keep my fleets clear of Sweden and the Baltic.

Germany remains the common obstacle. Are you willing to pressure from A PAR or A GAS this autumn, while I threaten Holland from the North Sea? I’ll keep my fleets away from Brest, Picardy, and the Channel; please tell me your plans.

France to Germany, Fall 1908. Units: A PAR, A GAS, F MAO, F BRE. Germany has A BUR, A MAR, A PIE, A RUH in the south-west. I still intend to stay out of Burgundy and Ruhr. Please confirm A MAR and A PIE will not move into Gascony, Spain or Piedmont-to-Marseille contact, and that no German unit enters Brest or Picardy this autumn.

France to England, Fall 1908. F MAO is heading for Portugal and Spain, not the Channel. F BRE stays in Brest. Please keep F ENG and F NTH away from Brest and Picardy, and tell me what your fleets in the North Sea and Barents are targeting this autumn.

France to Italy, Fall 1908. I'm focused on Spain and Portugal, and I have no interest in Tunis or the Adriatic. A WES and A TUN are your concern. Would you agree to keep F WES out of the Gulf of Lyon and the Spanish coast, leaving western Mediterranean spaces to us both?
Your F KIE now threatens a German center. Are you intending to hold KIE this fall? I will defend it; if you withdraw, I’ll keep F HOL clear of your centers and we can avoid escalating over Belgium.

A SIL and A UKR are close to my eastern centers. Are you planning any moves against Berlin or Munich this fall? I’ll keep my units out of Russian centers if you keep your armies clear of German territory.
My A PIE and A TYR are not targeting your centers this fall. Please keep A VEN and A TUN clear of Piedmont and Marseille; are you planning any move toward my western units?

Italy to Germany: Fall 1908. Your A PIE and A MAR are still next to my Piedmont and Tunis. I'm keeping A TUN and F WES out of Marseille and Burgundy. Confirm both stay out of Piedmont and Tunis this fall, and tell me whether A TYR is gone for good, since your board lists no unit there now.

Your F KIE is well placed against Germany. I can pressure A BER from A SIL; are you planning to hold KIE or move against another German center? I’ll keep A FIN clear of Sweden and avoid your northern fleets.

Your A BER is the key obstacle on my western front. I’m considering pressure from A SIL this fall. Are you holding Berlin, and will your eastern units stay out of Russian centers? I’m not looking to widen the front beyond that.

I intend to keep the southern front quiet this fall: A RUM, A SEV, and F BLA will stay out of Bulgaria, Constantinople, Armenia, and the Black Sea. Please keep A BUL out of Rumania and F ANK out of the Black Sea.

Turkey to Russia: Fall 1908. Your A RUM is now adjacent to my A BUL and CON. Confirm in writing that A RUM, A SEV and F BLA will not enter Bulgaria, Constantinople or Armenia this fall. If you hold, my F RUM-area units stay put and F ANK stays out of the Black Sea. Any move on Bulgaria will be met immediately.

Turkey to Austria: Fall 1908. Are A SER and A BUD still planning nothing against Bulgaria or Greece? I am holding A BUL and A GRE. If Russia moves on Rumania or Galicia, I suggest we coordinate to hit A RUM together. Tell me your plan first.

Turkey to Italy: Fall 1908. F NAP and A VEN have kept off Greece and Albania, as agreed. I am holding my Ionian and Adriatic positions. Please confirm F WES and A TUN stay out of Spain and Marseille this fall so we both keep focus north and west.

Austria to Turkey: Fall 1908. My A SER and A BUD have no plans against Bulgaria or Greece and will hold this fall. I agree Russia's A RUM is the threat to both of us. If it moves on Rumania-adjacent squares or Galicia, I am open to coordinating a strike on it. I will tell you before any change in my Balkan posture. Keep A BUL out of Serbia and Trieste as well.
I’ll keep F NTH and F BAR away from Brest, Picardy, and the Channel. Germany is still the target: please move A PAR or A GAS against a German position if you can, and tell me which one you choose.

I’ll use F NTH to threaten Holland; F KIE will not move against another German center this autumn. A SIL’s pressure on A BER would complement that well. My fleets will stay clear of Sweden and the Baltic.

I intend to contest Holland from F NTH, and I can’t promise to withdraw F KIE while your forces threaten my position. If F HOL leaves Holland and A BEL stays defensive, we can discuss de-escalation, but I won’t leave your centers unpressured.

France to England, Fall 1908. I am not sending A PAR or A GAS into Belgium or Burgundy. My plan is Spain and Portugal with A GAS and F MAO. F BRE stays in Brest. Your North Sea attack on Holland is your own affair, and I will not support it. Keep F ENG and F NTH away from Brest and Picardy, and we both do well.
A PIE will stay out of Piedmont and Tunis this fall. Germany has no A MAR; A TYR is still present, but will not move toward Trieste or Venice. Please keep A TUN and F WES clear of my western units.
A BOH is no longer in my forces, and I have no unit in SIL. A TYR will stay out of Trieste this fall. Please keep A VIE and A BUD out of German territory as proposed.
A PIE will stay out of Piedmont, and no German unit will enter Gascony, Spain, Brest, or Picardy this autumn. I have no A MAR; please continue keeping A PAR and A GAS clear of Burgundy and Ruhr.

F KIE is already occupied by your fleet, so F HOL cannot withdraw there. I intend to keep F HOL clear of your centers and A BEL defensive. Please keep F KIE out of German territory and avoid contesting Holland.

A BER will defend Berlin this fall. My eastern units will stay out of Russian centers; please keep A SIL and A UKR out of German territory, especially Berlin and Munich, so we can avoid widening the front.

Italy to France: I'm not planning any move toward Spain or Portugal. I'd rather keep F WES and A TUN focused on Tunis and the central Mediterranean, but I can't promise to abandon the Western Mediterranean entirely. Let's both keep our fleets out of each other's zones, and I'll watch Gulf of Lyon traffic on my side.

Italy to Turkey: Confirmed for now. F NAP and A VEN stay off Greece and Albania, and I expect your fleets to stay out of the Ionian and Adriatic. F WES and A TUN are not moving toward Spain or Marseille this fall. Keep your focus on Russia in the north.

Italy to Germany: A TUN and F WES will not enter Marseille or Burgundy this fall. I'm not moving against Piedmont or Tunis from my side either, and I'll keep A VEN in Venice. Your A TYR is no longer on the board, so I take it you have moved it. Let's keep the north and west separate.
A RUM and A UKR will stay out of Galicia and Serbia this fall. A SIL will move against Berlin, while A FIN will stay clear of Sweden and your territory. I’ll keep the southern front quiet as agreed.
Confirmed: A RUM, A SEV and F BLA will stay out of Bulgaria, Constantinople and Armenia this fall. Please keep A BUL out of Rumania and F ANK out of the Black Sea, as agreed.
I’ll use A SIL to pressure Berlin this autumn, not A WAR. Your F NTH can threaten Holland; I’ll keep A FIN clear of Sweden and won’t interfere with your fleets. What are you doing with F KIE?

A SIL will move against Berlin; A UKR will stay clear of German territory, and I’m not moving against Munich. I’m not targeting your other centers this fall. Keep your units out of Russian centers, as agreed.

Turkey to Austria: A BUL is holding and will stay out of Serbia and Trieste this fall. A GRE holds too. I am not planning any move against Serbia. In return, tell me plainly if A SER or A BUD moves toward Bulgaria or Greece, and we will coordinate against any Russian push into Rumania or Galicia.

Austria to Russia: Spring 1909. Your A RUM, A GAL and A PRU sit beside my border with A BUD, A SER and A VIE. Plainly: will A GAL and A RUM stay out of Galicia and Serbia this spring? If you confirm, I keep A BUD and A VIE out of Russian territory and do not move on Rumania.

Austria to Germany: Spring 1909. Your A RUH, A MAR and A BER are near my western border. Will you confirm no move into Tyrolia or Bohemia against Vienna this spring? I will keep A VIE out of German territory and hold A BUD. Tell me plainly what A BEL and A HOL do.

Austria to Turkey: Spring 1909. A SER and A BUD hold this spring and will not move toward Bulgaria or Greece. Please confirm A BUL stays out of Serbia and Trieste. If Russia's A RUM moves on Rumania or Galicia, I am ready to coordinate a strike on it with you.

I intend to contest Holland again with F NTH, and F KIE can reinforce the pressure. Will F HOL leave Holland this spring, and what are A BEL and A RUH doing? If you withdraw F HOL and keep A BEL out of my centers, we can discuss easing the northern front.

Can we coordinate pressure on Germany this spring? I can target Holland from F NTH; please tell me whether A PRU or A SIL can attack or support pressure on Berlin. I’ll keep my fleets clear of Sweden and Russian centers.

Germany remains my focus in the north. Are A PAR or A GAS positioned to pressure a German center this spring? I’ll keep F WAL and my other fleets away from Brest, Picardy, and the Channel; please share your plans.

France to Italy, Spring 1909. Your F WES is the western Mediterranean question. I plan A GAS to Spain and F MAO to Portugal, and I will not enter Tunis or the Adriatic. Please confirm F WES stays out of the Gulf of Lyon and Spanish coast this spring, and I will keep my fleets off Tunis and Naples.

F NTH can take Holland if F HOL is unsupported. I’m prepared to keep A BEL defensive and F HOL in Holland this spring if you leave Holland alone and keep F KIE out of German centers. Can we agree to avoid fighting over Holland this turn?

A PRU remains a direct threat to Berlin. I will defend Berlin and keep A MAR/A RUH out of Russian territory; please keep A PRU out of Berlin and A RUM clear of German centers this spring. Can we keep this front quiet?

I propose we keep our border quiet this spring: A MAR will stay out of French territory, and A RUH/A BEL will stay out of Burgundy and Picardy. Please keep A PAR and A GAS out of German centers and let me know if you intend to move against Belgium.

Italy to France, Spring 1909: I'll keep F WES out of Spain and Gulf of Lyon traffic toward Marseille, but I need Tunis secure. Will you confirm A PAR and A GAS stay out of Burgundy and Piedmont, and tell me if F POR heads for Spain?

Can we coordinate pressure on Germany again? I’m considering using A PRU against Berlin; are you planning to contest Holland or another German center with F NTH or F KIE? I’ll keep A FIN clear of Sweden and my units clear of your centers.

What are A BER and your other units doing this spring? A PRU remains in position to pressure Berlin. I’m willing to keep A UKR clear of your centers if you keep your forces out of Russian territory, but I can’t promise to leave PRU idle.

Can we renew the quiet-front understanding this spring? I’ll keep A RUM and A SEV out of Bulgaria and Constantinople, and F BLA out of the Black Sea. Please keep A BUL out of Rumania and F ANK out of the Black Sea; tell me if your plans have changed.

Turkey to Russia: Spring 1909. Your A RUM, A SEV and F BLA are adjacent to my A BUL and CON. You have promised to hold; I will hold A BUL and F ANK. Confirm in writing that A RUM stays out of Bulgaria and Constantinople, and tell me now if you plan Rumania or Sevastopol moves against me.

I won't agree to leave Holland alone while F HOL remains there. F NTH will contest Holland this spring, and F KIE will stay put rather than enter another German center. Keep A BEL defensive and don't target my centers; we can discuss de-escalation if you withdraw F HOL.

Yes—I'll contest Holland from F NTH, while F KIE stays in place and clear of German centers. A PRU moving against Berlin would complement the pressure; please do so if you can. I'll keep my fleets away from Sweden and Russian centers.

France to Italy, Spring 1909. I confirm A GAS heads for Spain and F MAO for Portugal. F POR stays in Portugal this spring. I will not enter Tunis, Naples or the Adriatic. Please keep F WES out of the Spanish coast and Gulf of Lyon, and we both gain from peace in the west.

France to England, Spring 1909. A PAR and A GAS are not moving against Germany this spring; my forces go south to Spain and Portugal. Keep your fleets off Brest and Picardy, and I will keep mine out of the Channel and North Sea. Good luck against Holland and Belgium.

France to Germany, Spring 1909. Agreed: I keep A PAR and A GAS out of Burgundy, Ruhr, Belgium and Munich this spring. My units head to Spain and Portugal. Please keep A MAR out of Gascony and Spain, and no German unit enters Brest or Picardy. Let us both keep the border quiet.

I confirm A BER and A MAR will not move into Bohemia or Tyrolia this spring. A BEL will support F HOL, and F HOL will hold Holland. A RUH will remain on the western front; please keep A VIE out of German territory.

I will keep F HOL in Holland, supported by A BEL, and keep A BEL out of your centers. I cannot leave Holland open while F NTH and F KIE threaten it. Please keep F KIE out of German territory and stand down from Holland so we can avoid a costly fight.

A BER will hold Berlin; A MAR and A RUH will stay out of Russian territory. I ask that A PRU stay out of Berlin and A RUM remain clear of German centers. I’m not seeking to widen our front, but I will defend Berlin.

Italy to France, Spring 1909: I can't confirm F WES stays out of the Gulf of Lyon and Spanish coast; I may need it to hold the western Mediterranean. I will not move F WES into Spain this spring, and I'll keep A TUN and my Naples fleet off your territory. In return, keep A GAS and F POR out of Piedmont, Tunis and the Adriatic, and we both keep Spain as a shared question rather than a fight.
A RUM will stay out of Serbia, and A GAL will hold rather than move into Serbia. I will keep A RUM out of your territory. Please keep A BUD and A VIE out of Russian centers as offered.
I’ll move A PRU against Berlin this spring, putting direct pressure on A BER. Your F NTH can contest Holland; I’ll keep A FIN clear of Sweden and my units clear of your centers.

Confirmed: A RUM will stay out of Bulgaria and Constantinople, and I am not planning a move against you from Rumania or Sevastopol this spring. Please keep A BUL out of Rumania and F ANK out of the Black Sea.
I’ll keep A RUM clear of German centers and A UKR out of your territory. I can’t promise to leave A PRU idle: I intend to move it against Berlin this spring. I’m not targeting your other centers.

Turkey to Austria: Spring 1909. A BUL holds this spring and will not enter Serbia or Trieste. I am not planning any move against Serbia. If Russia's A RUM moves on Rumania or Galicia, I agree we coordinate a strike on it. Tell me before any change to A SER or A BUD.

Turkey to Russia: Spring 1909. A BUL and F ANK hold this spring, and F ANK stays out of the Black Sea. I expect A RUM, A SEV and F BLA to stay out of Bulgaria, Constantinople and Armenia. Any move into those will be met at once. I will decide my fall plans after I see your spring orders.

Austria to Russia: Fall 1909. Your A RUM sits next to my Serbia and Bulgaria-facing units. Will A RUM and A UKR stay out of Galicia and Serbia this fall? I keep A BUD, A SER and A VIE out of Russian territory. Also, what does A GAL intend against Galicia? Plain answers please.

Austria to Germany: Fall 1909. Thank you for the spring confirmation. Will A BER and A MAR stay out of Bohemia and Tyrolia this fall, and will A RUH avoid Burgundy-to-Munich moves against me? I keep A VIE out of German territory. Tell me what A BEL and F HOL do this fall.

Austria to Turkey: Fall 1909. A SER and A BUD hold again this fall, no move toward Bulgaria or Greece. Please confirm A BUL stays out of Serbia and Trieste. If Russia's A RUM moves on Rumania or Galicia, we strike it together. Tell me before any change on your side.

Your A BEL and F HOL stopped my Holland attack last spring. What are you planning for F HOL and A BEL this autumn? I’m prepared to keep F KIE out of your centers if you’ll withdraw F HOL or agree to a clear de-escalation; otherwise I’ll keep contesting Holland.

Your forces are now in BOH and BUL, while Germany holds BEL, HOL and BER. Can you pressure MUN or BER this autumn? I’m considering another attack on Holland from F NTH, but it will need more than one unit to dislodge their defense. What are your plans?

Germany remains a major obstacle to both of us. Are A PAR or A GAS willing to pressure BUR or MUN this autumn? I’ll keep my fleets away from Brest, Picardy and the Channel; let me know your intentions before I commit to another Holland attack.

France to Italy, Fall 1909. I still want Spain and Portugal, and I won't touch Tunis or the Adriatic. Your F WES is the only western question. Confirm F WES stays out of Spain and the Gulf of Lyon this autumn and I will keep A GAS and F POR away from Piedmont and Tunis.

France to Germany, Fall 1909. A PAR and A GAS stay out of Burgundy, Ruhr, Belgium and Munich. Please keep A MAR out of Gascony and Spain, and no German unit enters Brest or Picardy. What are A BUR and A BEL planning this autumn?

France to England, Fall 1909. My fleets stay on the Iberian side, and F BRE remains in Brest. Keep your fleets off Brest and Picardy. Tell me if your North Sea attack on Holland will hit Belgium, so I can plan accordingly.

F NTH and F KIE bounced against F HOL last spring with A BEL supporting. I propose we stop contesting Holland this fall: keep both fleets out of HOL and German centers, and I’ll keep A BEL defensive and F HOL out of your centers. Can you agree?

Your A BOH is now close to Munich, while A UKR is near our southern border. I’ll keep German units out of Russian centers. Please keep A BOH out of Munich and Berlin and A UKR out of German territory this fall; are you planning otherwise?

With A MAR now in Piedmont, I propose keeping the western border quiet this fall: I’ll keep A PIE out of French territory and German units out of Gascony and Picardy. Please keep A PAR and A GAS out of Burgundy, Ruhr, and Munich; can we agree?

Italy to France, Fall 1909: Your A GAS to Spain is fine by me, but I need F WES to hold the Gulf of Lyon and Western Med. Confirm A PAR and A GAS stay out of Piedmont and Tunis, and that F POR does not go to Spain. I will keep A TUN and NAP off your land this fall.

Italy to Germany, Fall 1909: Your A BUR and A PIE sit close to my Piedmont and Tunis. Confirm A PIE stays out of Piedmont and Tunis, and that A BUR does not enter Marseille. In return A TUN and F WES stay out of Marseille and Burgundy. Tell me plainly what A BEL and A BER plan this fall.

Italy to Turkey, Fall 1909: Thank you for keeping clear of the Adriatic and Ionian. I am keeping F NAP and A VEN off Greece and Albania. I am watching Russia's build-up on your northern border too. Would you consider a joint push against Russia's southern holdings, Rumania and Sevastopol, while we both keep Italy and Greece quiet?

Let’s keep coordinating against Germany. I have A BOH and A LVN positioned near German centers; which center are you targeting with F NTH and F KIE this fall? I can apply pressure where it best complements your move.

A BUL is now Russian, though Bulgaria remains yours by ownership. I’m considering my fall move there; will you contest it, or can we avoid a southern war? Please keep A CON and A GRE from attacking Bulgaria, and tell me your plans for F ANK.

The front has shifted: A BOH and A LVN are near your centers, while England has been pressing Holland. Are you defending Berlin or another center this fall? I’m open to limiting the conflict, but need to know whether your units will threaten my centers.

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1909: Your A RUM sits next to my A BUL and CON, and your A UKR and A BUL-adjacent units are close. I will hold A BUL and F ANK. Tell me plainly whether A RUM or A UKR moves against Bulgaria, Constantinople or Armenia this fall. Silence will be read as a threat.

I’m not planning to hit Belgium from F NTH; my focus is still Holland. Could A PAR or A GAS pressure Burgundy this autumn, or otherwise threaten a German center? I’ll keep my fleets away from Brest, Picardy, and the Channel.

I can’t agree to leave Holland uncontested while F HOL remains there. I’m prepared to keep F KIE out of your centers, but unless F HOL withdraws or we reach a clear de-escalation, I’ll continue to contest Holland. Please keep A BEL defensive.

I’m focusing F NTH on Holland, with F KIE available to support that pressure. Could A BOH pressure Munich, and can A LVN threaten Berlin via Prussia? Either would complement my move. I’ll keep F STP clear of Sweden and my forces away from your centers.

France to Italy, Fall 1909. Yes, A GAS goes to Spain and F POR stays in Portugal this autumn. I will not move A PAR or A GAS toward Piedmont or Tunis. Keep F WES out of Spain and the Gulf of Lyon, and we both stay out of each other's way.

France to Germany, Fall 1909. Agreed on the western border. A PAR and A GAS stay out of Burgundy, Ruhr, Belgium and Munich this autumn. Please keep A MAR out of Gascony and Spain, and no German unit enters Brest or Picardy. A PIE should stay out of Piedmont-to-Marseille moves as well.

France to England, Fall 1909. I will not send A PAR or A GAS against Burgundy or Munich. My fleets stay on the Iberian side and F BRE stays in Brest. Your Holland attack is your own affair. Keep your fleets off Brest and Picardy and we remain at peace.

Agreed to keep the western border quiet. A BUR will stay out of Burgundy, Ruhr and Munich, and A PIE will stay out of French territory; no German unit will enter Brest or Picardy. Please keep A PAR and A GAS out of German centers.
A BER and A BUR will stay out of Bohemia and Munich, and A PIE will not enter Tyrolia. A BEL will support F HOL, while F HOL holds. Please keep A VIE out of German territory.

A PIE is already in Piedmont, so I can't promise it will stay out of Piedmont; I will not move it to Tunis or any Italian center. I will keep it out of Marseille. A BEL supports F HOL and A BER defends Berlin. Please keep A TUN and F WES out of German territory.

A BER will defend Berlin; German units will not enter Russian centers. Please keep A BOH out of Munich and Berlin, and A LVN out of Berlin. I want to avoid widening the front, but I will protect my centers.

I won't withdraw F HOL while F NTH can attack it, and A BEL will continue to support it. I will keep A BEL out of English centers and F HOL out of yours. If you keep F KIE out of German centers and stop attacking Holland, we can de-escalate.

Italy to France, Fall 1909: A GAS to Spain is acceptable to me. F WES will not enter Spain this autumn, but I will keep it in the Western Mediterranean and Gulf of Lyon as needed. Please keep A PAR and A GAS out of Piedmont and Tunis, and F POR out of Spain while you take it with A GAS. I will keep A TUN and NAP off your land.
A RUM will stay out of Serbia, and A UKR will stay out of Galicia and Serbia. A GAL no longer exists; that army moved to BOH in spring. I’m not planning an attack on your centers this fall.

A RUM and A UKR will not move against Bulgaria, Constantinople or Armenia this fall. A BUL is Russian and I intend to keep it there; please keep A CON and A GRE from attacking it. What is F ANK doing?

I’m not planning to send A UKR into German territory. I can’t promise A BOH will stay out of Munich or Berlin; England is pressing Holland and I’m considering pressure on your southern centers. Are you willing to keep your forces away from Russian centers?

I can pressure Munich with A BOH this fall; A LVN is not positioned to support that move. I don’t have a move on Berlin from BOH. F NTH’s Holland attack will need support, so coordinate with F KIE if you can.

Turkey to Russia: Your A BUL is in Bulgaria, which is my home ownership. I will not accept that. A CON and A GRE will contest Bulgaria this fall, and F ANK stays out of the Black Sea. Withdraw A BUL now or we fight in the south. Tell me plainly what A RUM and A UKR do next.

Turkey to Austria: Russia has moved A BUL into Bulgaria, so our understanding on Bulgaria is void. I will strike it with A CON and A GRE. Please move A SER or A BUD against A RUM this fall, as we agreed, so Russia cannot reinforce the Balkans. Confirm you will do so.

Turkey to Italy: I welcome a joint push against Russia's southern holdings. Russia has taken Bulgaria, and I will hit it now. Keep F NAP and A VEN off Greece and Albania, and keep F WES and A TUN focused westward toward Spain. Once Bulgaria falls, we can discuss Rumania and Sevastopol.

Austria to Turkey: Spring 1910. Russia's A BUL is now a real threat to both of us. I will not move A SER or A BUD against you. I propose A SER and A BUD hold or strike A RUM if Russia's A RUM moves toward Rumania. Confirm you will hit A BUL in Bulgaria this spring with A CON and A GRE.

I’m reassessing the northern front. What are F HOL and A BEL doing this spring? I’m considering F NTH to HOL with support from F KIE; if you’ll keep A BEL defensive and avoid my centers, tell me what de-escalation you can offer.

Can we coordinate pressure on Germany this spring? I can attack HOL from F NTH with support from F KIE. Can A PRU move against BER, with A BOH supporting, or what are those units planning? I’ll keep my fleets clear of Russian centers.

What are your plans around the Channel and northern France this spring? I’m focused on Germany and can keep my fleets away from Brest and Picardy if you’ll keep F BRE and your armies clear of my centers.

France to Italy, Spring 1910. I keep A GAS and F POR out of Piedmont and Tunis, and my fleets stay off the Adriatic. Your F WES is still the question: will it stay out of Spain this spring? I'm moving toward Spain and Portugal, not Italian land.

France to England, Spring 1910. My fleets stay on the Iberian side and F BRE stays in Brest. I have no plan against Burgundy this spring. Keep your fleets out of Brest, Picardy and the Channel, and tell me whether F NTH moves toward Holland or Belgium.

France to Germany, Spring 1910. Our western border agreement stands: A PAR and A MAR stay out of Burgundy, Ruhr, Belgium and Munich. Please keep German units out of Gascony, Spain, Brest and Picardy. Tell me what A MUN and A BEL intend this spring.

F NTH can dislodge F HOL if supported, but A BEL can defend Holland. I propose a spring stand-down: keep F NTH and F KIE out of HOL and German centers, and I’ll hold F HOL and keep A BEL defensive. Can you agree?

A PRU threatens Berlin and A BOH threatens Munich. I will defend both centers and keep German units out of Russian centers. Please keep A PRU out of Berlin and A BOH out of Munich this spring; are you willing to avoid a German front?

Russia’s A BOH threatens Munich, while A PRU is near Berlin. I’ll defend my centers and keep German units out of your territory. Please keep A VIE and A GAL out of German centers this spring; can we maintain a quiet border?

Italy to Turkey, Spring 1910: Agreed on Russia. I'm keeping F NAP and A VEN off Greece and Albania. Are you pushing from Constantinople and Smyrna toward Rumania or Sevastopol this spring? Please confirm your fleets stay out of the Adriatic and Ionian.

I can coordinate pressure on Germany again: A PRU can attack Berlin and A BOH can attack Munich. Are F NTH and F KIE targeting Holland this spring, and can you support the Holland attack? I’ll keep A FIN clear of Sweden.

Our forces remain in direct contact around Berlin and Munich. Are you willing to agree that German units stay out of Russian centers this spring? I’m considering pressure from A PRU and A BOH; tell me plainly which centers you intend to defend.

A BUL is still Russian, and I recognize Turkey owns Bulgaria. I’m not promising to withdraw it, but want to avoid a wider southern war. What will A CON, A GRE, and F ANK do this spring? I’ll keep A RUM out of Bulgaria and Constantinople.

Turkey to Russia, Spring 1910: A BUL is Russian and I will contest it. A CON and A GRE attack Bulgaria this spring unless A BUL withdraws. Your A RUM and A UKR are the threat to my ownership. Tell me plainly now whether A RUM moves on Bulgaria, Constantinople or Armenia.

Turkey to Austria: Spring 1910. I am striking Bulgaria now with A CON and A GRE. Please move A SER or A BUD against A RUM this spring as agreed, so Russia cannot reinforce the Balkans. Confirm in writing what you will do.

Turkey to Italy: Spring 1910. Bulgaria is my target now. Keep F NAP and A VEN off Greece and Albania, and keep F WES and A TUN pressing Spain. Once Bulgaria is retaken, we can discuss Rumania and Sevastopol together.

Austria to Turkey: Spring 1910. I will not move A SER or A BUD against your Bulgaria strike. Striking A RUM is a separate matter I have not decided; I will tell you before any move. Good luck taking A BUL with A CON and A GRE.

Austria to Germany: Spring 1910. A VIE and A GAL will not enter German centers this spring. I keep A VIE out of Munich and Berlin. Russia's A BOH is your problem to answer; if you move on Bohemia or Tyrolia, I will defend. Tell me what A BEL and F HOL do.
F NTH is moving against Holland, with F KIE supporting; I am not targeting Belgium. My fleets will stay out of Brest, Picardy, and the Channel, and I ask that your forces remain clear of my centers.

Yes: F NTH attacks HOL with support from F KIE. Please send A PRU to BER and A BOH to MUN as proposed; that will divide German defenses. I’ll keep my fleets clear of Russian centers, including Sweden.

I can’t agree to a stand-down while F HOL remains in place. F NTH will attack HOL with F KIE supporting. I’ll keep F KIE out of your centers otherwise; please keep A BEL defensive and stay clear of English centers.

France to England, Spring 1910. My armies stay clear of your centers and F BRE stays in Brest this spring. I have no plans against Edinburgh, Lyon or Kiel. Keep your fleets out of Brest, Picardy and the Channel, and let me know if F NTH or F KIE turns toward Belgium or Holland so I can adjust my Iberian moves.
The agreement stands. A MUN and A BEL will hold defensively; German units will stay out of Gascony, Spain, Brest, and Picardy. Please continue keeping A PAR and A MAR out of German centers.

I’ll defend Berlin and Munich, and German units will stay out of Russian centers. Please keep A PRU out of Berlin and A BOH out of Munich; I’m not looking to widen the conflict, but cannot leave either center undefended.

F HOL will hold, and A BEL will support its defense. I’ll keep A BEL out of English centers. If F NTH and F KIE stay out of Holland and German centers, we can avoid a clash; I can’t promise to abandon Holland while it’s threatened.

Italy to France, Spring 1910: I will keep F WES out of Spain this spring as you asked. Your A GAS and F POR staying out of Piedmont and Tunis is what I need. Keep your fleets off the Adriatic and Tunis, and we can revisit Spain later.

Italy to Turkey, Spring 1910: F NAP and A VEN stay off Greece and Albania. Rumania and Sevastopol are a fair target once Bulgaria is secured. Keep your fleets out of the Adriatic and Ionian, and tell me which of your armies moves north first.

A RUM will not move against Bulgaria, Constantinople, or Armenia this spring. I intend to keep A BUL, despite your attacks; I won’t pretend our positions are settled. I’ll keep F BLA out of the Aegean, but cannot offer a broader southern guarantee.

I won’t agree to keep A PRU out of Berlin or A BOH out of Munich. I intend to attack Berlin from PRU and Munich from BOH; these are pressure, not a promise to widen into other German centers. I appreciate your assurance that German units stay out of Russian centers.

Yes: A PRU will attack Berlin and A BOH will attack Munich. I can’t support your Holland attack from those positions, but these moves should draw German defenders away from HOL. Coordinate F NTH and F KIE as you judge best; A FIN will stay clear of Sweden.

Turkey to Austria: Spring 1910. Yes, A CON and A GRE will attack A BUL in Bulgaria this spring. I will not move toward Serbia or Trieste. Please move A SER or A BUD against A RUM as agreed, so Russia cannot reinforce the Balkans. Confirm in writing before the orders are set.

Turkey to Italy: Spring 1910. My A CON and A GRE are going into Bulgaria, and F ANK stays in the eastern Black Sea approaches, not toward Rumania. Keep F NAP and A VEN off Greece and Albania as promised. Rumania and Sevastopol can wait until Bulgaria is settled.

Turkey to Russia: A BUL is in my home territory and I will contest it this spring with A CON and A GRE. F ANK stays out of the Black Sea. Withdraw A BUL to Rumania or Serbia and this can stop there. Your A RUM must not enter Bulgaria or Constantinople. Silence will be read as refusal.

Austria to Russia: Fall 1910. Your A BOH, A BUL and A PRU are pressing my borders. Will you confirm A MOS, A BUL and A BLA keep out of Galicia, Rumania and Serbia this fall? I keep A VIE, A BUD and A SER out of Russian centers. Plain answer on A BUL's intentions, please.

Can we coordinate another attack on Germany this fall? I’m considering F NTH to HOL with F KIE supporting. Please tell me whether A PRU will attack BER and A BOH will pressure MUN; those moves would keep German forces occupied. I’ll keep my fleets clear of Russian centers.

The Holland dispute remains unresolved after F HOL and A BEL stopped my attack. I’m considering another move against HOL this fall. Are you willing to withdraw F HOL or agree to a concrete de-escalation? I’ll keep F KIE out of your other centers and ask that A BEL stay clear of English centers.

I’m focused on Germany again this fall. I plan to keep my fleets away from Brest, Picardy, and the Channel. Can you keep F BRE and your armies clear of my centers, and are you considering any pressure on Germany that might complement my move against Holland?

France to Italy, Fall 1910. I am still moving my armies toward Spain and Portugal, not Tunis or Piedmont. Please confirm F WES stays out of Spain and the Gulf of Lyon this autumn, and that A TUN and NAP stay off Marseille and Gascony. I will hold my fleets off the Adriatic.

F HOL and A BEL are still positioned to defend Holland. Can we avoid another costly attack this fall? Keep F NTH and F KIE out of HOL; I’ll keep A BEL defensive and all German units out of English centers. If you intend to attack anyway, please say so plainly.

A BOH and A PRU still threaten Munich and Berlin. I will defend both, and German units will stay out of Russian centers. Can you keep A BOH out of Munich and A PRU out of Berlin this fall? I’d rather contain the front than widen it.

I propose we maintain our western-border agreement this fall: German units stay out of French centers and French units stay out of Belgium, Ruhr, and Munich. Please confirm your intentions for A PAR and A MAR.

Italy to France, Fall 1910: Your A PAR and A MAR are on my western border. I want A TUN and F WES secure. Confirm A MAR stays out of Piedmont and Tunis and F POR does not move to Spain while I hold the Western Med. In return I keep F WES out of Spain and Marseille.

Italy to Turkey, Fall 1910: Russia's A BUL is gone, so Bulgaria is contested. Are you retaking Bulgaria with A CON and A GRE? I will keep F NAP and A VEN off Greece and Albania. Once Bulgaria is settled, let's agree a concrete line against Rumania and Sevastopol.

Italy to Germany, Fall 1910: Tell me plainly where A MUN and A BEL go. I keep A TUN and F WES out of German land. Please keep A PIE out of Piedmont and Tunis and A MUN out of Tyrolia-Venice, since A VEN is staying home.

Let’s renew pressure on Germany this fall. F NTH can attack HOL with F KIE supporting; I can send A PRU to BER and A BOH to MUN again. Can you commit to the Holland attack, and keep F NWG clear of Norway?

I’m considering renewed pressure on BER and MUN from A PRU and A BOH. Your spring assurance was to keep German units out of Russian centers; will that hold this fall? I’m not looking to widen into other German centers if you leave Russian territory alone.

A BUL held through your spring attack, and I intend to keep it Russian this fall. I’ll keep A RUM out of Bulgaria and Constantinople, but cannot promise to withdraw A BUL. Are A CON and A GRE attacking Bulgaria again, or will you leave it alone?

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1910: A BUL is still yours and I will not let it stand. My A CON and A GRE hit Bulgaria this fall. Withdraw A BUL to Rumania now and Turkey stays out of Rumania and Sevastopol. Refusal means war in the south, and your A MOS and A PRU would be better used against Germany.

I’ll attack HOL again with F NTH supported by F KIE; the dispute remains unresolved, and I won’t pretend otherwise. Keep A BEL defensive and German units clear of English centers, and I’ll keep F KIE out of your other centers. A withdrawal from HOL is still the clearest way to de-escalate.
Yes, I’ll attack HOL with F NTH supported by F KIE. Please send A PRU to BER and A BOH to MUN as proposed, and keep F NWG clear of NOR. I’ll keep my fleets clear of Russian centers.

France to Italy, Fall 1910. A MAR will not move to Piedmont or Tunis. F POR stays in Portugal this autumn, and I do not plan to move F POR to Spain while you hold the Western Med. Please keep A TUN and NAP off Marseille and Gascony as well. We both stay in our own lanes.
A BEL will support F HOL, and A MUN will hold Munich. I’ll keep A MUN out of Tyrolia and Venice, and A BEL out of your centers. Please keep A TUN and F WES out of German territory.

That assurance still holds: German units will stay out of Russian centers. I will defend Berlin and Munich; A PRU and A BOH remain threats, so I can’t leave either center undefended. I’d prefer you keep them out this fall and avoid widening the conflict.

I won’t withdraw F HOL while it remains threatened. A BEL will support its defense, and I’ll keep German units out of English centers. If F NTH and F KIE stay out of Holland and German centers this fall, we can avoid another costly clash.

Italy to France, Fall 1910: I will keep F WES out of Spain and the Gulf of Lyon this autumn. Your A PAR and A MAR must stay out of Piedmont and Tunis, and F POR stays out of Spain while I hold the Western Med. Keep your fleets off the Adriatic and we have peace in the west.

A MOS and F BLA will stay out of Galicia, Rumania and Serbia. A BUL will hold rather than enter your territory. A BOH is directed against Munich, not Vienna or Budapest; I cannot promise that the pressure on your borders will end.

A BUL will hold; I will not withdraw to Rumania. I expect A CON and A GRE to attack again, and will defend Bulgaria. A RUM will stay out of Bulgaria and Constantinople, and F BLA will not enter the Aegean. Your threat to Rumania and Sevastopol leaves little basis for trust.

German units staying out of Russian centers is welcome, but I will not leave Berlin and Munich unpressured. A PRU will attack Berlin and A BOH will attack Munich this fall. I’m not seeking to widen into other German centers if you keep your assurance.

Yes, A PRU will attack BER and A BOH will attack MUN again. Please make the supported attack on HOL with F NTH and F KIE as proposed. I’ll keep A NOR out of Sweden; I can’t direct your F NWG, but hope you keep it clear of Norway.

Turkey to Russia: Withdrawing A BUL is the only thing that stops this. My A CON and A GRE will attack Bulgaria this fall, and I will not pretend otherwise. Your A RUM staying out of Bulgaria and Constantinople is noted; keep it there and I will keep F ANK out of the Black Sea. Your move.

Turkey to Italy: Yes, A CON and A GRE are retaking Bulgaria this fall. Thank you for keeping F NAP and A VEN off Greece and Albania. I will keep my fleets out of the Adriatic and Ionian. Once Bulgaria is settled, let us agree a concrete line against Rumania and Sevastopol, starting with who moves first.

Austria to Turkey: Spring 1911. Russia's A BUL and A BOH threaten us both. I will hold A SER and A BUD this spring. Will you confirm A CON and A GRE keep striking Bulgaria, and A ANK stays out of Armenia-facing moves against me? Tell me plainly before any change to your Serbia or Trieste posture.

Can we renew pressure on Germany this spring? I’m considering F NTH to HOL supported by F KIE. Will A PRU attack BER and A BOH pressure MUN again? I’ll keep my fleets clear of Russian centers, including NOR.

I’m considering another supported attack on HOL with F NTH and F KIE. Are F HOL and A BEL staying in place, or will you offer a concrete de-escalation? I’ll keep F KIE out of your other centers and ask that German units stay clear of English centers.

I’m focused on Germany this spring and plan to keep my fleets away from Brest, Picardy, and the Channel. Can you keep F BRE and your armies clear of English centers, and let me know whether you intend to pressure Germany?

France to England, Spring 1911. My armies stay clear of your centers and F BRE stays in Brest. I am not planning moves against Belgium or Holland. Keep your fleets out of Brest and Picardy. I am watching Spain and Portugal, so tell me if F MAO or F WAL shifts toward Iberia.

France to Germany, Spring 1911. Our western border deal stands: A PAR and A MAR stay out of Burgundy, Ruhr, Belgium and Munich. Please keep German units out of Gascony, Spain, Brest and Picardy. What do A BEL and A MUN intend this spring?

France to Italy, Spring 1911. I hold A MAR and A PAR away from Piedmont and Tunis, and F POR stays out of Spain this spring. Please keep F WES and A TUN off Marseille and Gascony. Let us both stay in our lanes while I deal with Spain next season.

Your repeated attacks on Berlin and Munich leave little room for détente. This spring I’ll defend both centers and keep German units out of Russian centers. Will you keep A PRU out of Berlin and A BOH out of Munich, or are you continuing the attacks?

F HOL remains exposed to F NTH and F KIE, and A BEL will continue supporting its defense. I’ll keep German units out of English centers. Are you still planning to attack Holland this spring, or can we agree to keep F NTH and F KIE out of HOL?
I propose keeping our western border quiet this spring: German units stay out of French centers, and A PAR and A MAR stay out of Belgium, Ruhr, and Munich. Can you confirm your intentions?

Italy to Turkey, Spring 1911: Bulgaria is secured by your side per our line. I hold F NAP and A VEN off Greece and Albania. Confirm A CON and A SMY stay south of Bulgaria, and that you move on Rumania or Sevastopol only together with me. Which army goes north first?

Italy to France, Spring 1911: Keep A PAR and A MAR out of Piedmont and Tunis, and F POR out of Spain while I hold the Western Med. I will keep F WES out of Spain and Marseille. Confirm your moves this spring in writing.

Italy to Austria, Spring 1911: I hold Venice and Naples and have no quarrel with you. Tell me whether A RUM and A SER stay on the Russian and Turkish fronts, and whether F TRI will move toward Venice. I will keep A VEN home unless you attack Tyrolia or Trieste.

Let’s renew pressure on Germany: I plan A PRU to BER and A BOH to MUN. Can F NTH and F KIE coordinate against HOL again? Please keep your fleets clear of Russian centers, especially Sweden and Norway.

I intend to continue pressuring BER and MUN from A PRU and A BOH. Your assurance that German units stay out of Russian centers remains important; will you maintain it this spring? I’m not seeking to widen the conflict beyond those fronts.

I expect you may again contest A BUL. I intend to defend it, with A RUM able to support from RUM and F BLA able to support from the Black Sea. Will A CON and A GRE leave Bulgaria alone this spring? I’ll keep A RUM out of Bulgaria and Constantinople.

Turkey to Russia, Spring 1911: Bulgaria is still contested, but I see your fleets and armies are needed against Germany. Offer: A BUL withdraws to Rumania and I keep A CON and A GRE home this spring. Otherwise A CON and A GRE hit Bulgaria. Tell me your answer before orders lock.

Austria to Italy, Spring 1911: I have no plan to move against Venice or Tyrolia. A SER and A BUD hold toward Turkey and Russia this spring. F TRI stays put and is not heading toward Venice. Keep A VEN and A ROM home and we remain at peace; tell me if your A PIE moves toward Tyrolia or Trieste.

F NTH will attack HOL with support from F KIE again this spring; your continued occupation and A BEL's support leave the dispute unresolved. I’ll keep F KIE out of your other centers, and ask you to keep German units clear of English centers. A concrete withdrawal from HOL would change the situation.

My fleets will stay clear of Brest, Picardy, and the Channel, and F MAO and F WAL are not shifting toward Iberia. Please keep your forces clear of English centers as promised. I’m coordinating pressure on Germany; let me know if your plans change.

Agreed: F NTH will attack HOL with F KIE supporting. Please send A PRU to BER and A BOH to MUN as planned. I’ll keep my fleets clear of Russian centers, including Sweden and Norway; please keep A SWE clear of Norway.

France to Germany, Spring 1911. Our western border deal stands. A PAR and A MAR will not enter Burgundy, Ruhr, Belgium or Munich. I expect German units to stay out of Gascony, Spain, Brest and Picardy in return. Your A BEL and A MUN are your business, but keep them off French centers.

France to Italy, Spring 1911. A MAR and A PAR will not move to Piedmont or Tunis, and F POR stays out of Spain this spring. Please keep F WES and A TUN off Marseille and Gascony. We remain in our own lanes for now.

France to England, Spring 1911. F BRE stays in Brest and my armies stay clear of your centers this spring. I am not planning moves against Belgium or Holland. Keep your fleets out of Brest and Picardy. If F MAO or F WAL heads toward Iberia, I will need to reconsider our arrangement.

Our western-border deal stands. A BEL will remain focused on Holland, and A MUN will defend Munich against A BOH. German units will stay out of Gascony, Spain, Brest, and Picardy; please keep A PAR and A MAR out of Belgium, Ruhr, and Munich.

F HOL and A BEL will stay in place to defend Holland; I won’t offer a withdrawal while F NTH and F KIE threaten it. German units will stay out of English centers. Keep F KIE out of my other centers and stay out of HOL if you want to avoid another clash.

I will maintain the assurance: German units will stay out of Russian centers. A PRU and A BOH continue to threaten Berlin and Munich, so I will defend both this spring. I’m not seeking to widen the conflict; please keep those attacks confined to BER and MUN.

Italy to France, Spring 1911: Agreed. F WES stays out of Marseille and Gascony and will not enter Spain while you keep A PAR, A MAR and F POR off Piedmont, Tunis and the Adriatic. I will watch for any fleet heading into the Gulf of Lyon. Please confirm your spring orders in writing so we both know where we stand.
I’m continuing the pressure: A PRU to BER and A BOH to MUN. Keep German units out of Russian centers, and I’ll keep this focused on those two fronts rather than widening it.
I will not withdraw A BUL to RUM; A BUL will hold, with A RUM and F BLA available to support. If A CON and A GRE attack Bulgaria, I will defend it. Keep your units out of RUM and the Black Sea.
Yes: A PRU to BER and A BOH to MUN again. Please have F NTH attack HOL supported by F KIE, and keep your fleets clear of Russian centers, especially NOR and SWE.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1911: Bulgaria is mine now, with A BUL, A CON and A SMY holding it. I have no army moving on Serbia or Trieste this spring. F ANK stays in the Black Sea and away from Armenia. Keep A RUM and A GAL pointed at Russia, not at Bulgaria. We both gain if Russia is pushed back north.

Turkey to Italy, Spring 1911: Confirmed. A CON and A SMY stay south of Bulgaria, and A BUL holds it. Rumania and Sevastopol are a joint move only, and I will not act there before we agree timing. Keep F NAP and A VEN off Greece and Albania as promised. I suggest A ROM and A TUN stay in the west for now.

Turkey to Russia, Spring 1911: Bulgaria is held by Turkey, and I will defend it. Your A RUM must stay out of Bulgaria and Constantinople. If F BLA stays out of the Aegean and A RUM stays north, F ANK stays in the Black Sea. Your armies are better used against Germany and Austria than in the Balkans.

Austria to Russia, Fall 1911: Your A BOH retreated to SIL, so Bohemia is open. Will A SIL and A PRU stay out of Bohemia, Galicia and Vienna this fall? I will keep A VIE, A BUD and A RUM out of Russian centers if you confirm plainly. Tell me what A FIN, A LVN and F ARM do.

F NTH and F KIE are still positioned to contest HOL. Are you willing to move F HOL out this fall and end the repeated clash? I can keep F KIE away from your other centers and will not target English centers; otherwise I expect the Holland dispute to continue.

Can we coordinate pressure on Germany again this fall? Are A PRU to BER and A SIL to MUN still your plans? I’m weighing F NTH to HOL supported by F KIE; please confirm your moves and keep your forces clear of English centers.
I intend to keep my fleets clear of Brest, Picardy, and the Channel this fall. Please keep F BRE and your armies clear of English centers as agreed. Are you still staying out of Belgium and Holland?

France to Italy, Fall 1911. Our lanes have held, but I am now moving on Spain. A PAR and A MAR stay off Piedmont and Tunis, but F POR goes to Spain this autumn. Keep F WES and A TUN out of Marseille and Gascony, and I will keep my fleets out of the Adriatic.

F HOL and A BEL can still defend Holland, but another supported attack will only prolong the stalemate. I’ll keep German units out of English centers; will F NTH and F KIE leave HOL alone this fall, and keep F KIE out of BER and MUN?

A BOH is now the main immediate threat to Munich. Please keep it out of MUN this fall; I’ll keep German units out of Austrian centers. Can we avoid opening another front while Russia and England are pressing us?

Your A PRU still threatens Berlin, while your former A BOH has retreated to SIL. I’ll continue keeping German units out of Russian centers, but please keep A PRU out of BER this fall. Can we contain the conflict rather than renew the attack?

Italy to Turkey, Fall 1911: Bulgaria is yours and I keep NAP and VEN home. Russia's A RUM route is open and Sevastopol is ripe, but I need a firm answer: will your A BUL or A CON strike Rumania this autumn, or do you want me to wait? Tell me which units go where so we avoid overlap.

Let’s keep pressure on Germany this fall. I can send A PRU to BER with A SIL supporting; please renew F NTH to HOL with F KIE supporting. Keep your fleets clear of NOR and SWE, and let me know if you expect Germany to move against Russian centers.

Bulgaria remains Russian, and I expect you may contest it again. I can keep A RUM out of BUL and CON; will A CON and A GRE leave BUL alone this fall? I’d rather avoid spending another season fighting over it while Germany remains a threat.

I’m prepared to continue pressuring BER from A PRU, with A SIL available to support. Your assurance that German units will stay out of Russian centers still matters; will you maintain it this fall? I’m keeping my focus on Berlin rather than widening the front.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1911: Bulgaria is held and my A CON and A SMY stay south. I will not move on Rumania or Sevastopol without you. Please confirm F NAP and A VEN stay off Greece and Albania this fall, and tell me whether A TYR threatens Austria's Trieste, since that changes Austria's posture toward me.

Austria to Germany, Fall 1911: I have no order to move into Munich or Bohemia this fall. My units stay on Austrian centers while Russia's A SIL is the real danger to both of us. If you keep A MUN and A BEL solid and German units out of Tyrolia and Vienna, I will do the same. Tell me what A BER and F HOL do so we can coordinate against Russia.

F NTH will again attack HOL with support from F KIE; your continued occupation leaves the dispute unresolved. I’ll keep F KIE away from BER and MUN, and expect German units to stay clear of English centers. Moving F HOL out would end this repeated clash.
Agreed: F NTH attacks HOL with F KIE supporting. Please send A PRU to BER with A SIL supporting as planned, and keep your forces clear of English centers. I’ll keep my fleets clear of NOR and SWE.

France to England, Fall 1911. F BRE stays in Brest this autumn and my armies stay clear of your centers. I am not moving against Belgium or Holland. Keep your fleets out of Brest and Picardy as agreed. I am now focused on Spain, so if F MAO or F WAL turns toward Iberia, our arrangement is off.

I’m not willing to move F HOL while F NTH and F KIE continue to contest it; A BEL will support its defense. I’ll keep German units out of English centers. If F KIE stays out of BER and MUN, and you leave HOL alone this fall, we can stop repeating this clash.

I’ll maintain my assurance: German units will stay out of Russian centers. A PRU supported by A SIL threatens Berlin directly, so I’ll defend BER and ask you to keep the attack confined there. Please do not widen the conflict; I have no designs on Russian territory.

Italy to France, Fall 1911: Noted that F POR moves to Spain. I will keep F WES out of Spain and Marseille as agreed, and A TUN stays out of Marseille and Gascony. But I expect your fleets to stay out of the Adriatic and Ionian, and your armies off Piedmont and Tunis. If you move on Spain, that is your business, not a reason for us to fall out.

Italy to Turkey, Fall 1911: Confirmed, F NAP and A VEN stay off Greece and Albania this fall. A TYR is not threatening Trieste; it sits on my northern border. I will not commit to Rumania yet. Let us agree that A BUL or A CON strikes Rumania only in Fall 1912 with my fleet support in the Adriatic, and Sevastopol after that. Tell me your Spring 1912 orders first.

I can keep A SIL and A PRU out of BOH, GAL, and VIE this fall. A FIN and A LVN will stay clear of your territory; F ARM remains in ARM. I ask that A RUM and your other units stay out of Russian centers, especially SEV and MOS.

I can’t promise to leave BER unpressured while you hold German units out of Russian centers. A PRU will attack BER, with A SIL supporting. I’m keeping this focused on Berlin; please maintain your assurance and don’t move against Russian centers.
Yes: A PRU to BER, with A SIL supporting. Please renew F NTH to HOL supported by F KIE, and keep your fleets clear of NOR and SWE. I’ll keep my forces clear of English centers.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1911: Thank you. A BUL holds Bulgaria, and A CON and A SMY stay south this autumn. I will not move on Rumania or Sevastopol alone. Let us agree on a joint spring 1912 move. I propose A BUL to Rumania with your support against Austria's RUM, with timing set in our next exchange. Please keep F NAP and A VEN off Greece and Albania.

Turkey to Russia, Fall 1911: Bulgaria is Turkish and will stay so, held by A BUL, A CON and A SMY. I will not contest it further if F ARM stays out of the Black Sea and your armies stay north against Germany. Turkey will not move on Sevastopol while that holds. Refusal means I keep my southern units ready.

Austria to Russia, Spring 1912: Your A SIL and A WAR are the threat to my Bohemia and Galicia. Confirm plainly that A SIL stays out of Bohemia and Galicia this spring and A WAR does not strike Galicia. In return my A RUM and A VIE stay off SEV and MOS. Your F BLA also stays out of Rumania.

Germany’s F HOL plus A BEL has repeatedly matched my supported attack. Can you pressure BER or MUN again this spring to pull German support away? I’ll renew pressure on HOL with F NTH and F KIE; I’ll keep my fleets clear of NOR and SWE.

Could you move A PAR to BEL this spring and help break Germany’s position while I contest HOL? I’ll keep my fleets clear of Brest and Picardy, and won’t move toward Iberia. Let me know if you’re willing to coordinate.

The HOL contest is stalemated. I’m willing to discuss a way out: would you move F HOL elsewhere this spring if I keep F KIE away from BER and MUN? Otherwise I expect the dispute to continue. I’ll keep English units clear of German centers other than HOL.

France to England, Spring 1912. F BRE stays in Brest and my armies stay clear of your centers. I am moving to take Spain, not Belgium or Holland. Keep your fleets out of Brest and Picardy. Your F MAO and F WAL stay in the Atlantic and Channel, and we both keep our promises.

F NTH and F KIE can keep forcing a bounce in HOL, but neither of us gains from repeating it. Will you leave HOL this spring and keep F KIE out of BER and MUN? I’ll keep German units out of English centers.
I expect A PRU to press BER again. I’ll keep German units out of Russian centers; please keep A PRU’s attack confined to BER and do not move A SIL into MUN. Can we avoid widening this front?

Please keep A BOH out of MUN this spring. Russia still threatens BER, and I need to concentrate on defending against that pressure. I’ll keep German units out of Austrian centers; let’s avoid opening another front.

Italy to Turkey, Spring 1912: I am not moving A VEN or F NAP toward Greece or Albania. Rumania is a Fall 1912 target for us, not Spring, since Austria's A RUM and A SER are still there. Before any joint move, tell me exactly which unit hits RUM and whether A SMY comes north to support it. I will keep my fleets out of the Ionian.
Can we renew coordinated pressure on Germany? I can send A PRU to BER and A SIL to MUN; will F NTH again attack HOL with F KIE supporting? Please keep your fleets clear of NOR and SWE.

I intend to keep pressure on BER and MUN with A PRU and A SIL. Please maintain your assurance that German units will stay out of Russian centers; are you planning to defend both cities or move against Russian territory?

I want to avoid opening a southern front while I deal with Germany. Will you keep F ANK and your armies out of Russian centers, especially SEV and RUM? I can keep F BLA and A RUM out of Turkish territory if we maintain that understanding.

Turkey to Italy, Spring 1912: Before any joint move on Rumania, I need certainty. Will F NAP and A VEN stay off Greece and Albania this spring? My A BUL, A CON and A SMY stay put for now. Confirm your Spring orders so we avoid overlap on Rumania and Sevastopol timing.

Turkey to Russia, Spring 1912: Your A BUL is still the sticking point. Withdraw it to Rumania and Bulgaria stays quiet this spring. Otherwise I cannot promise my southern units stay home. Keep F BLA out of the Aegean and A RUM out of Bulgaria and Constantinople.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1912: I have no army moving on Serbia or Trieste this spring. Keep A RUM and A SER pointed at Russia's northern and Rumanian positions. Tell me your Spring plan so we both stay aligned against Russia.

Austria to Turkey, Spring 1912: I have no order against Serbia or Trieste this spring. A SER and A RUM stay aimed at Russia's Rumanian and northern positions. I will not strike Bulgaria. If Russia moves on Rumania, we can coordinate then. Tell me your Spring orders against Russia before you commit.

Austria to Germany, Spring 1912: My A BOH is not ordered toward Munich this spring. I will keep Austrian units off German centers as long as you keep yours off Vienna and Tyrolia. Russia's A SIL is the danger to both of us, so please hold A MUN and A BEL solid and tell me what A BER and F HOL do.

I’m willing to coordinate against Germany. Please move A PAR to BEL this spring while I renew the F NTH–HOL attack supported by F KIE. I’ll keep my fleets out of Brest and Picardy and won’t move toward Iberia; please keep A PAR out of English centers.

I won’t leave HOL uncontested while F HOL remains there and A BEL supports it. I’ll renew the F NTH attack with F KIE support, and keep F KIE away from BER and MUN. Moving F HOL out this spring would end the dispute; I’ll keep English units clear of your other centers.
Agreed: I’ll renew F NTH to HOL with F KIE supporting. Please send A PRU to BER and A SIL to MUN as proposed, and keep your forces clear of English centers. I’ll keep my fleets clear of NOR and SWE.

France to England, Spring 1912. I will not move A PAR to Belgium; my plan is Spain, which is where my army goes this season. F BRE stays in Brest and my armies stay off your centers. Keep your fleets out of Brest and Picardy and we remain on good terms. Germany's Low Countries are your business.

I’m defending both BER and MUN this spring. German units will stay out of Russian centers; I have no plan to move against Russian territory. Please keep A PRU focused on BER and A SIL out of MUN so we can contain this conflict.

I can move F HOL to HEL if F NTH and F KIE both leave HOL unoccupied and F KIE stays out of BER and MUN. With F NTH still positioned to attack HOL, withdrawing would simply hand you the center. I’ll keep German units out of English centers.

Italy to Turkey, Spring 1912: Confirmed. My F NAP and A VEN stay off Greece and Albania this spring, and I am not moving toward the Ionian. Rumania is a Fall 1912 joint target, not Spring. Keep A BUL, A CON and A SMY where they are for now. When we plan the autumn strike, tell me exactly which unit hits RUM and whether A SMY comes north to support it. Mind your own Aegean borders meanwhile.

I’ll keep A SIL out of BOH and GAL, and A WAR will not attack GAL this spring. A RUM and A VIE must stay out of SEV and MOS; I’ll keep F BLA out of RUM. I can’t promise to leave the eastern front undefended if your units move against Russian centers.

I’ll keep F BLA out of the Aegean and A RUM out of BUL and CON. I’m not withdrawing A BUL to RUM: it is a Russian unit, and I need to retain that position. Keep F ANK and your armies out of SEV and RUM, and we can avoid opening a southern front.

A PRU will press BER, and I intend to use A SIL against MUN. I’m keeping the pressure focused on German centers for now. Maintain your assurance that German units will stay out of Russian centers, and tell me plainly whether you intend to defend BER and MUN or move against Russia.

Yes, I’ll renew pressure on Germany: A PRU to BER and A SIL to MUN. Please send F NTH to HOL with F KIE supporting again, and keep your fleets clear of NOR and SWE. I’ll keep Russian forces clear of English centers.

Turkey to Italy, Spring 1912: A BUL, A CON and A SMY stay put this spring, so no move on Rumania yet. I agree Rumania is a Fall 1912 target, with A BUL striking RUM supported by your fleets and A SMY coming north if needed. Keep F NAP and A VEN off Greece and Albania as agreed, and send me your Spring orders first so we avoid overlap.

Austria to Russia, Fall 1912: Your A SIL and A PRU are next to Bohemia and Munich. Confirm plainly that A SIL, A PRU and A FIN stay out of Bohemia, Galicia and Vienna this fall. I will keep A VIE, A BUD and A RUM off SEV, MOS, WAR and STP. Are you moving on Rumania or Galicia?

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1912: Russia's A UKR and A WAR are the threat to both of us. Will A ANK and A SMY strike Sevastopol or Rumania this fall? I will hold A RUM and A BUD and not move toward Bulgaria or Constantinople. Tell me your orders plainly.

Austria to Germany, Fall 1912: A BOH will not move on Munich this fall. Keep A BER and A MUN aimed at Russia's A PRU and A SIL, and keep German units out of Tyrolia and Vienna. Tell me what F HOL and A BEL do so we stay coordinated.

Can we coordinate pressure on Germany again this fall? I can renew F NTH to HOL with F KIE supporting. Are A PRU and A SIL still able to pressure BER and MUN? Please keep your forces clear of English centers and let me know your plans.

The HOL contest remains unresolved. If you move F HOL to HEL this fall, I can keep F KIE away from BER and MUN; otherwise I expect F NTH to HOL supported by F KIE. I’ll keep English units clear of your other centers, and expect German units to stay clear of English centers.

I’ll keep English fleets clear of Brest and Picardy and won’t move toward Iberia. Please keep your units clear of English centers and let me know whether you intend to stay out of Belgium and Holland this fall.

France to England, Fall 1912. I am committed to Spain and Portugal, not Belgium. My A PAR and A MAR stay away from your centers and F BRE stays in Brest. Your F NTH and F KIE pressure on Holland is your affair. Please keep your fleets out of the Channel and Picardy as agreed, and tell me if you plan any move on Brest.

France to Italy, Fall 1912. I am taking Spain this autumn with F POR and holding my armies off Piedmont and Tunis. Please keep F WES and A TUN out of Marseille and Gascony. I will keep my fleets out of the Adriatic and Ionian. Tell me your intentions for the Western Med.

France to Germany, Fall 1912. Our western border holds: A PAR and A MAR stay out of Burgundy, Ruhr, Belgium and Munich. In return, keep German units out of Gascony, Spain, Brest and Picardy. What are your plans for A BEL and A MUN this autumn?

Russia’s A PRU and A SIL are still threatening BER and MUN. I’ll defend both German centers and keep German units off Austrian centers. Can you keep A BOH out of MUN and coordinate pressure against Russia rather than open a German-Austrian front?

Your A PRU and A SIL threaten BER and MUN again. I intend to defend both, and German units will stay out of Russian centers. Will you keep A PRU focused on BER and A SIL out of MUN this fall, so we can avoid widening the conflict?

The HOL contest remains a stalemate. I’ll keep F HOL defended with A BEL and stay out of English centers. Will you leave HOL uncontested this fall and keep F KIE away from BER and MUN? If not, please say whether you intend to renew the supported attack.

Italy to Turkey, Fall 1912: Time to strike. Your A BUL takes Rumania this autumn, supported by my fleets. Confirm A SMY moves north to Bulgaria as backup. My A VEN and F NAP stay off Greece and Albania, and I will not move on Trieste or Greece. Tell me your orders first so we avoid overlap.

Let’s keep pressure on Germany this fall. I can send A PRU to BER and A SIL to MUN; can you attack HOL with F NTH supported by F KIE again? Please keep your fleets clear of NOR and SWE, and I’ll keep Russian units clear of English centers.

I want to avoid a southern front while pressing Germany. F ARM will stay out of the Black Sea, and A RUM will stay out of BUL and CON. In return, keep your units out of SEV and RUM this fall. Can you confirm?
I’ll keep A SIL and A WAR out of BOH and GAL, and F ARM out of RUM this fall. Please keep A RUM and A VIE out of SEV and MOS; I want to avoid an eastern clash while I focus on Germany.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1912: Rumania strike is on. A BUL moves to RUM, supported by your fleets from the Adriatic, and A SMY comes north to CON-BUL if needed. Please confirm your Fall orders now, including F NAP and A VEN staying off Greece and Albania, so we avoid overlap.

Austria to Russia: I will not order A BOH, A VIE or A RUM into Galicia or Russian centers this fall, but I cannot bind my future orders beyond this turn. Your A SIL, A PRU and A FIN staying out of Bohemia, Galicia and Vienna is what I need confirmed plainly.
