Your forces have overwhelming pressure on my western centers. What are your Spring 1945 intentions for F BEL, F NTH, A LON, and the German front? I can keep A BER and A MUN out of your centers if you will keep F BEL and F NTH from supporting attacks on MUN or BER.

With England holding BEL and pressing toward Germany, can we keep our frontier quiet this spring? I will keep A PIC out of your centers; please keep A PAR and F BRE from entering or supporting attacks on PIC, MUN, or BER. What are your plans?

England's nine centers and nearby forces make it the immediate threat to my survival. Are your A TYR, A TRI, and A VIE still staying clear of German centers this spring? I can keep A MUN and A BER off your frontier if you will avoid supporting attacks on them.

Italy to Austria, Spring 1945: Your A TYR is still next to Venice. Confirm in writing it stays out of VEN and PIE this spring. In return I keep A VEN and A ROM off TRI and SER. Also, do you plan any move against Greece or Tunis-facing waters with A ALB or A BUL?

Italy to Turkey: Our Balkan talks have held. Austria's A BUL and A ALB sit near Greece; I will not move toward GRE or SER. Please confirm A MOS and F ANK stay off Greece and the Aegean, and tell me what you plan against Austria this spring.

Italy to England: F TUN and my fleets stay off Spain, Portugal and the English-held waters as agreed. Please keep F NTH and F IRI away from the Mediterranean and Iberia this spring. I am still assessing Austria and will tell you if my plans change.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1945: Your A BUL and A BUD must stay off CON, SEV, ANK and WAR. I will keep my forces off BUD, VIE, SER and TRI this spring, but only if your units hold their current positions. Tell me your spring orders first and I will answer on that basis.

Turkey to England: Your A EDI, A LON and F NTH are far from my centers, and I want it kept that way. My focus is Austria's Balkan and Galician holdings, not your northern or western centers. Let us both keep fleets out of the Black Sea and Eastern Mediterranean, and tell me if your Baltic or Scandinavian plans touch STP or MOS.

Turkey to Germany: Spring 1945, my A WAR and A MOS press Austria's Galician and Balkan holdings, aiming at GAL and BUL. Your A MUN and A BER should go toward BOH and SIL, not my centers. Keep out of WAR and MOS and we stay clear of each other.

Austria to France, Spring 1945: I hold A TYR and A VEN in place this spring and will not enter Piedmont or Marseille. Our quarrel is Italy and Turkey, not you. Keep your A PAR and A MAR home and we stay clear of each other.

Austria to Italy, Spring 1945: A TYR will not enter VEN or PIE this spring, and A ALB and A BUL will not move toward Greece or Tunis-facing waters. Keep A VEN and A ROM off TRI and SER and we remain at peace.

Austria to Turkey, Spring 1945: A BUL, A SER and A BUD will not enter CON, SEV, ANK or WAR this spring. My spring orders are defensive. A WAR and A MOS must stay out of GAL. Confirm that and we keep the Balkan and Black Sea borders quiet.

Austria to Germany, Spring 1945: A TYR, A TRI and A VIE will not enter or support attacks on MUN, BER or HOL this spring. Keep your armies off BOH and our frontier and we stay quiet. England is a shared problem; I will not oppose you on the western front.

F NTH and F IRI will stay out of the Channel, Biscay, MAO, and Iberian approaches; no English unit will approach BRE or your southern centers. F BEL and A LON are directed against Germany, not France. Please keep your forces away from BEL and English centers.

F NTH and F IRI will stay out of the Mediterranean and Iberian waters this spring. I have no plans against your centers; my immediate pressure is on Germany. Please keep F TUN and your other units away from English-held waters.

My Baltic and Scandinavian plans do not touch MOS, and I have no move against STP this spring. I’ll keep my fleets out of the Black Sea and eastern Mediterranean. Are A WAR and A MOS still committed against Austria? Austria’s Balkan centers remain the main threat.

F BEL and F NTH will press your western position, and I cannot promise to keep them from supporting against MUN or BER. A LON will stay focused on the German front, not your English-center-facing units. I’ll keep my armies out of PIC; if you leave a German center uncontested, tell me which one.

France to England: Spring 1945. My western units stay home while your fleets stay out of Biscay, MAO and the Channel and no English unit approaches SPA or BRE. Your F BEL and A LON are a concern, since England holds BEL now and pressing Germany is your business, not mine. Confirm your Spring orders in writing and I will keep F BRE, A PAR, A MAR and F POR in place.
Agreed: A MUN will move to BOH and A BER to SIL, away from your centers. A PIC will stay clear of WAR and MOS. Please keep A WAR and A MOS focused on Austria and out of German territory.

I cannot leave BER or MUN open; those are my remaining defenses. I will keep A BER and A MUN out of English centers and will not support attacks on your units. Please keep F BEL and F NTH from supporting attacks on MUN or BER, and keep your armies out of PIC.

Italy to France, Spring 1945: I will keep A VEN and F GOL out of Marseille and Piedmont this spring as agreed. F TUN will stay out of Spanish and Marseille waters. Keep A MAR and A PAR home. I am also watching English movements toward Iberia and will tell you if any Italian plan changes.

Turkey to Italy: I will keep A MOS and F ANK away from Greece and the Aegean this spring. My pressure goes against Austria's Galician and Balkan holdings, not toward GRE or SER. Keep your fleets clear of CON and the Aegean and we stay friends. Tell me if your A VEN moves toward TRI or TYR.

Turkey to Austria: I make no written promise on A WAR or A MOS this spring. Your A BUL, A SER and A BUD must stay off CON, SEV, ANK and WAR. If they do, I will not move onto BUD, VIE, SER or TRI. Show me your spring orders and I will answer on that basis.

Turkey to England: My A WAR and A MOS are aimed at Austria's Galician and Balkan holdings, not your centers. I will keep A ANK away from your northern areas. Keep F BAR and F NTH out of the Black Sea and away from STP and MOS, and we will both gain while Austria is checked.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1945: My A BUL, A SER and A BUD stay off CON, SEV and ANK. Your A GAL, A WAR and A MOS are the real question. Tell me your fall orders for A GAL and A SEV before I commit. If you leave GAL alone, I will leave your Black Sea and Anatolian centers alone too.

I’m positioned to take BER from F BAL, with F HEL able to support. I propose you avoid contesting BER this fall and keep your units out of English centers; I’ll leave MUN alone for now. Are you willing to let BER change hands without a costly fight?

I intend to press Germany this fall, not France. Please keep A PAR, A MAR and F BRE away from BUR, MUN and English centers; I’ll keep my western fleets clear of your waters and units. Can we keep the western front quiet while Germany is settled?

Are you continuing your Balkan and Turkish campaign this fall? I’m focused on the German front and have no plans in the Adriatic or Mediterranean. Please keep your units away from BER and the English-held north while I move against Germany.

France to England, Fall 1945: Your F NAO and F NWG must stay out of Biscay, MAO and the Channel, and no English unit approaches SPA or POR. My F BRE, A PAR, A MAR and F POR stay home. Confirm your Fall orders for F BEL and A LON so I know whether Germany or the low countries are your target.

France to Italy, Fall 1945: Your A APU and F GOL must stay out of Marseille, the Gulf of Lyon coast and Piedmont, and F TUN out of Spanish and Marseille waters. I keep A MAR and A PAR home. Tell me your Fall orders for A VEN and A ROM now, and whether Austria's A VEN is a threat to you.

France to Austria, Fall 1945: You hold 7 centers and Italy is the target for both of us. A TRI and A VEN must not enter Piedmont or Marseille. I keep A PAR and A MAR home. Tell me whether A VEN moves against Italy this Fall or stays put.

Your nine centers make you the immediate threat to everyone. I cannot leave MUN, BER, or KIE open, but propose we avoid wasting moves against each other: what are your Fall targets, and will you keep F HOL and F HEL from supporting attacks on German centers? I’ll keep A BUR and A BOH out of your centers.

England is at nine centers and pressing Germany. Can you use A TRI or A VIE to threaten its advance through the German front this fall, while keeping your units out of MUN, BER, and KIE? I’ll keep A BOH and A BUR off your centers; coordinating against England is our best chance to prevent a solo.

England’s nine centers make it the immediate danger. Will you turn A PAR or A MAR toward the English front rather than press German centers? I can keep A BUR out of your territory; let’s coordinate to deny England another center and prevent a solo.

Italy to Austria, Fall 1945: Your A VEN is still in Venice, which is my home center, so I need it gone. Tell me plainly whether A VEN and A TRI are moving against Italian holdings this fall. I will keep A ROM and F TUN out of TRI and SER only if you confirm A VEN retreats or leaves Italy alone.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1945: Keep A BUL, A BUD and A SER off CON, SEV, ANK, WAR and MOS. I will keep A WAR, A MOS and A GAL off BUD, SER, TRI and VIE while that holds. Tell me your A ALB and A VEN orders first. Our shared interest is Italy's Adriatic holdings, not each other.

Turkey to Italy, Fall 1945: I will keep A MOS, A WAR and F ANK away from GRE and the Aegean. Keep F TUN and F GOL out of the Eastern Mediterranean and away from CON. What are your A APU and A ROM orders? I am watching Austria's A VEN near TRI and will tell you if that changes.

Austria to Italy: A VEN is my unit and I will decide its fall moves privately. I make no promise to retreat or leave Italy alone. A TRI and A TYR stay where they are for now. Keep A ROM and F TUN away from TRI and SER and we stay at peace this fall.

F BEL and A LON are aimed at Germany, not the low countries or France. I will keep F NAO and F NWG out of Biscay, MAO and the Channel, and no English unit will approach SPA or POR. Please keep your units away from German centers and English centers so I can settle the German front.

I intend to take BER from F BAL, with F HEL supporting. F HOL and F HEL will not support attacks on MUN or KIE, but F HEL must support my move on BER. I will leave MUN alone this fall and keep my units out of your other centers; please do not contest BER or enter English centers.

France to Germany: I am not turning A PAR or A MAR toward the English front this fall. My units stay home while England's fleets stay out of Biscay and the Channel. I will not support or enter Burgundy against you, but if England presses Germany, I will not be the one to lose Belgium's neighbours to a solo. Keep A BUR out of Marseille and Gascony and we stay clear.

France to England, Fall 1945: I hear you intend to press Germany, which suits me. I keep F BRE, A PAR, A MAR and F POR home. Hold your word: F NAO and F NWG stay out of Biscay, MAO and the Channel, and no English unit approaches SPA or POR. Your F BEL and A LON are your business against Germany; I will not interfere if you leave my western centers alone.

No. BER is one of my last three centers, and I cannot consent to surrender it while you stand at nine. I will defend it this fall. If you truly intend to leave MUN alone, keep F HEL from supporting F BAL into BER; I will keep my forces out of English centers.

Italy to France, Fall 1945: My A APU and F GOL will stay out of Marseille, the Gulf of Lyon coast and Piedmont this fall, and F TUN stays out of Spanish and Marseille waters. A ROM holds in Rome. Austria's A VEN sits in my home center and I am watching it closely. Keep A MAR and A PAR home and tell me if English fleets approach Iberia.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1945: My A GAL stays put this fall, and A WAR and A MOS will not enter GAL. Your A BUL, A BUD and A SER must stay off CON, SEV, ANK, WAR and MOS. Show me A ALB and A VEN orders first; if A VEN heads for APU or ROM, I will not object. Italy is the shared target, not each other.

Austria to Turkey, Spring 1946: My A BUL, A SER and A BUD stay off CON, SEV, ANK and WAR. I want A GAL and A VIE to hold and I will not strike Rumania this spring. Are your A RUM and A SEV holding too? Tell me your orders first so we avoid a clash in the Balkans.
I intend to keep the western front quiet and will not approach BRE, POR, or your southern centers. Please keep your units out of BEL and English centers while I press Germany in the north.

I am positioned to attack DEN with F HEL, with F HOL able to support. I will not promise to leave it alone. Please keep A DEN from moving against English centers; are you willing to avoid a costly contest there?

I remain focused on the north and have no plans against your centers or eastern waters. Are you still pressing Austria? I would prefer your forces remain committed there rather than moving toward the English north.

France to England, Spring 1946: Your fleets are now in Bar, Fin and Hel, far from my coasts. Confirm your Spring orders in writing. If you keep F HOL and F KIE on the German front and no English unit enters Biscay, MAO or the Channel, my F BRE, A PAR, A MAR and F POR stay home. What is A LVP doing?

With eight centers, you are the main threat to a solo. What are your Spring targets? I’ll defend my remaining centers and won’t enter English centers; can you keep F HEL and F KIE from supporting attacks on BER or MUN this turn?

England’s position threatens all of us. Will you use A PAR to pressure PIC or Burgundy and avoid supporting English attacks on German centers? I’ll keep A BEL and A SIL clear of French territory; let’s coordinate to slow England.

England’s growing lead is the danger to us all. Can you move A VIE or A TRI toward BOH to pressure the German front and deter English expansion? I’ll keep A SIL away from your centers; please avoid supporting English attacks on BER or MUN.

Italy to Austria, Spring 1946: Your A VEN is in my home center and I need it gone. Tell me plainly whether A VEN, A TRI or A BUD move against Italian holdings this spring. If A VEN leaves Italy, I keep A ROM and F TUN away from TRI and SER. Confirm in writing.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1946: The board has changed since our old promises. Tell me your current orders for A BUD, A BUL, A SER and A TRI before I commit. I will not move onto your centers unless you move onto mine first, and I expect no A GAL or A WAR entries from you either.

Austria to Turkey, Spring 1946: My A BUD, A BUL and A SER are holding this spring and will not enter CON, SEV, ANK or WAR. A VIE and A GAL hold too. I will not strike Rumania. Confirm your A RUM, A SEV and A WAR orders first, and we keep the Balkan border quiet.

Austria to Italy, Spring 1946: A VEN stays in Venice this spring and I will not support any move against your holdings from it. A TRI and A BUD hold position. I cannot promise more than that while Italy's fleets sit next to my Adriatic coast. Keep A ROM and F TUN away from TRI and SER.

Austria to Germany, Spring 1946: A TRI and A VIE hold this spring and will not enter BOH or attack MUN, BER or HOL. I cannot spare a move toward BOH while Turkey and Italy press me. Keep your armies off my frontier and we stay quiet.

A LVP will stay on the German front; I have no plans to move it toward your centers. F HOL and F KIE remain focused on Germany, while my fleets stay out of Biscay, MAO, and the Channel. Please keep your units away from BEL and English centers as agreed.

My targets are DEN and the German north; I cannot promise to keep F HEL or F KIE from supporting attacks on your centers. I will keep my forces out of English centers. Are you planning to contest DEN, or would you rather preserve your units for the rest of the front?

France to Germany, Spring 1946: I will not move A PAR toward PIC or Burgundy this spring. My units stay home while I watch England's fleets. I will not support English attacks on German centers, but I also will not sign a pact that ties my hands. Keep your units out of Gascony and Marseille, and we stay clear.

France to England, Spring 1946: Noted that F BAR, F FIN and F HEL are far from my coast. I keep F BRE, A PAR, A MAR and F POR home. Your F HOL and F KIE on the German front are your business. Any English unit entering Biscay, MAO or the Channel, or approaching SPA or POR, ends this understanding. Your A LVP should stay in England.

I can't leave DEN undefended or agree to hand it over; it is one of Germany's last centers. I will keep A DEN out of English centers. If you keep F HOL from supporting F HEL into DEN, I will not move A DEN against your centers this turn. Otherwise I will contest the attack.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1946: My A RUM and A SEV will hold this spring. I make no move on your Balkan or Galician centers while your A BUL, A SER and A BUD stay off CON, SEV, ANK and WAR. Hold A GAL and A VIE as you say, and we will both see a quiet spring.

Turkey to England: Thank you. I remain focused on Austria's Balkan and Galician holdings and have no plan against the northern powers. Keep your fleets out of the Black Sea and eastern Mediterranean and we will stay at peace.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1946: Your A RUM, A SEV and A MOS are sitting on my Balkan and Galician edge. My A BUD, A BUL and A SER stay off CON, SEV, ANK and WAR. Tell me your fall orders for A RUM and A GAL-facing units now. If you leave GAL and BUL alone, I will hold VIE and TRI and not strike RUM.

Austria to Italy, Fall 1946: A VEN is still in Venice and I will not promise its retreat. A TRI and A BUD hold. If Italy keeps A ROM and F TUN away from TRI and SER, I will not support any move against your holdings from VEN this fall.

Austria to Germany, Fall 1946: A VIE and A TRI hold this fall and will not enter BOH or attack MUN, BER or HOL. Keep your armies off my frontier and out of TYR and GAL, and we stay quiet while England presses us both.

I’ll keep my fleets out of the Channel, Biscay and MAO, and will not approach your centers. Please keep your armies away from BEL and English centers while I settle the German front. Are you planning any moves into German centers this fall?

Your A SWE and A MUN leave the north exposed. I intend to press German centers this fall; I won’t move against English-held centers. Are you planning to contest my position in DEN or KIE, or can we avoid spending units on attacks against each other?

You now have seven centers and are close to the lead. Are you staying focused on Austria this fall, or do you intend to move north toward my centers? I have no plans against your centers or eastern waters if you keep your forces away from the English north.

France to England, Fall 1946: Your fleets have taken Hol, Kie and Bel, and England now sits at eight centers. Spain and Portugal remain my concern. Confirm in writing that F BOT and F NWG stay out of Biscay, MAO and the Channel this fall, and that no English unit approaches SPA or POR. In return my F BRE, A PAR, A MAR and F POR stay home. Your move against Germany is your business.

You have eight centers and can still reach 18 only by expanding. I cannot give up DEN or MUN. What are F DEN and A SWE doing this fall? Keep F DEN out of KIE and support no attack on MUN, and I will keep A RUH and A BOH out of your centers.

England remains the chief solo threat. Please keep A PAR and A MAR out of BUR and RUH and do not support English attacks on German centers. I will keep A RUH and A BOH out of French territory; can you maintain that neutrality this fall?

My units are not moving against your centers. With England at eight and pressing Germany, can you keep A TRI and A VIE from supporting English attacks on German centers, and focus your pressure on Turkey instead? I will keep A BOH and A MUN off your frontier.

Italy to Austria, Fall 1946: A VEN is still in my home center and I will not accept that as a standing arrangement. Either A VEN retreats out of Italy or I will treat it as hostile. Confirm in writing whether A VEN and A TRI stay off Italian holdings this fall. I will hold A ROM and F TUN off TRI and SER only if you do.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1946: Your A BUD, A BUL and A SER have held off CON, SEV, ANK and WAR, and I appreciate that. Confirm your fall orders now. If your units stay put, my A RUM, A SEV and A WAR will not enter BUD, SER, TRI or VIE. Any move onto RUM, SEV or WAR breaks this understanding.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1946: A BUD, A BUL and A SER will hold and stay off CON, SEV, ANK and WAR. A TRI and A VIE also hold. Your A RUM, A SEV and A WAR must not enter BUD, SER, TRI or VIE, and please keep A MOS and A GAL-facing units out of GAL. If you move onto RUM or SEV from your side, we are no longer at peace.

Austria to Italy, Fall 1946: A VEN stays in Venice this fall and I make no promise on its retreat. A TRI and A BUD hold. I will not support any move against your holdings from VEN. Keep A ROM and F TUN away from TRI and SER and we remain at peace.

Austria to Germany, Fall 1946: A VIE and A TRI hold this fall and will not enter BOH, MUN, BER or HOL. I will not support English attacks on German centers. Keep your armies out of TYR and GAL and we stay quiet while England presses us both.

F BOT and F NWG will stay out of the Channel, Biscay and MAO, and no English unit will approach SPA or POR this fall. Please keep A PAR, A MAR and F POR away from BEL and English centers. I am not coordinating moves against German centers with you.

F DEN will not move to KIE, and I will not support an attack on MUN. I intend to use A SWE against your remaining northern position, however. Please keep A RUH and A BOH out of English centers; I will keep my forces out of yours.

France to Germany, Fall 1946: I will keep A PAR and A MAR out of Burgundy and the Ruhr this fall, and I will not support English attacks on your centers. Our neutrality holds as long as your A RUH and A BOH stay out of Gascony, Marseille and Piedmont. I am watching England's fleets closely, so do not give me reason to reconsider.

France to England, Fall 1946: Congratulations on Hol, Kie and Bel. My F BRE, A PAR, A MAR and F POR stay home this fall if F BOT and F NWG stay out of Biscay, MAO and the Channel and no English unit approaches SPA or POR. Any breach ends our understanding. My armies stay out of Belgium and your centers, and I have no intention of moving into German centers this fall.
Understood. Germany will keep A BOH and A MUN off your frontier and avoid TYR and GAL. Please do not support English attacks on German centers; England's expansion is a danger to both of us.

I will contest your position in DEN and KIE rather than stand by while you take German centers. I will keep A RUH and A BOH out of English centers, but I cannot promise to leave MUN undefended while you press Germany.

Italy to Austria, Fall 1946: Your A VEN has sat in my home center for too long. I will hold A ROM and F TUN off TRI and SER this fall only if A VEN is ordered out of Venice to a non-Italian territory, which you can do by retreating or moving it now. Without that, I cannot treat your Adriatic presence as peaceful. Confirm your orders for VEN and TRI in writing before we finalize our moves.

Turkey to Austria, Fall 1946: My A RUM, A SEV and A WAR will not enter BUD, SER, TRI or VIE this fall while your A BUD, A BUL and A SER stay off CON, SEV, ANK and WAR. I am not moving onto GAL in this message; I make no promise beyond this fall. Any move onto RUM, SEV or WAR by your units breaks this understanding.

Austria to Turkey, Spring 1947: My A BUD, A SER and A BUL will hold, staying off CON, SEV, ANK and WAR. Tell me your A RUM, A SEV, A WAR and A MOS orders now. I want no unit of yours entering BUD, SER, TRI or VIE, and I will not move onto RUM while you keep that promise.

I’m considering my northern moves this spring. I can keep F NTH and F SKA away from your centers if you keep A BER, A HOL, A MUN and A NOR out of English centers. Are you planning to contest KIE or DEN, or can we avoid wasting units on attacks against each other?

With 8 centers, your expansion is the main strategic concern for me. Are you still pressing Austria, or do you intend to move north toward English or German centers? I have no plans in your direction if your forces stay away from the north.

I intend to keep the western front quiet and stay away from your centers this spring. Please confirm that F BRE, A PAR, A MAR and F POR will remain away from BEL and English centers. Are you planning any moves against Germany?

France to England, Spring 1947: Your F BAL, F SKA and A YOR are far from my coast, which I welcome. Confirm in writing that F NTH and A WAL stay off Biscay, MAO and the Channel this spring, and no English unit approaches SPA or POR. My F BRE, A PAR, A MAR and F POR stay home in return. Any breach ends our understanding.

France to Italy, Spring 1947: My A MAR and A PAR stay home, and F POR and F BRE hold. I ask that your F TUN and F GOL keep out of Spanish and Marseille waters, as you promised. Let us both watch Austria's A VEN and A TRI. If you need a Western Mediterranean ally, I am open to talks.

With both of us at six centers, a fight only helps Turkey. This spring, please keep F SKA and F BAL off German centers and do not support attacks on BER, HOL, or NOR. I will keep A MUN, A HOL, and A BER out of English centers. What are your targets?

Can we maintain the neutrality we discussed? Please keep A PAR and A MAR out of BUR and RUH and do not support English attacks on German centers. I will keep A MUN and A HOL out of French territory. England and Turkey are the threats to both of us.

Please keep A TRI and A VIE from entering BOH or supporting attacks on German centers this spring; I will keep A MUN and A BER off your frontier. With England and Turkey both strong, I hope we can avoid opening another front.

Italy to Austria, Spring 1947: A VEN is still sitting in Venice, my home center. I will treat it as hostile unless it leaves Italy now. Tell me plainly if you will move A VEN out this spring. If it does, I keep A ROM and F TUN off TRI and SER.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1947: Your units are now listed as A BUD, F GRE, A SER, A TRI, A VIE. Tell me your exact spring orders for GRE, SER and TRI. I will keep my armies off your home centers while your A SER and F GRE stay out of BUL and CON. Any unit entering BUL or SEV breaks this.

Austria to Italy, Spring 1947: A VEN stays in Venice this spring. I will not support any move against your holdings from it. A TRI and A SER will hold and not enter ADR or your territories. Keep A ROM and F TUN off TRI and SER and we remain at peace. I make no promise on VEN's future beyond this spring.

Austria to Turkey, Spring 1947: A BUD, A SER and A BUL will hold. Our understanding stands while your A RUM, A SEV, A WAR and A MOS stay off BUD, SER, TRI and VIE and do not enter BUL or SEV from BUL's side. My F GRE holds in Greece and stays out of BUL and CON. Any move onto RUM or WAR by you breaks this.

Austria to Germany, Spring 1947: A TRI and A VIE hold this spring and will not enter BOH or support attacks on German centers. Keep A MUN and A BER out of TYR and GAL and we stay quiet. England's fleets in the North Sea are a common problem, but I will not commit my armies to your front this year.

Confirmed: F NTH and A WAL will stay out of Biscay, MAO and the Channel this spring, and no English unit will approach SPA or POR. Please keep your forces away from BEL and English centers. I am not coordinating an attack on Germany with you.

I can keep F SKA and F BAL away from German centers this spring if your armies stay out of English centers. My targets are the northern position and protecting my current gains; I will not support attacks on BER, HOL or NOR. Are you leaving DEN and KIE uncontested?

France to England, Spring 1947: Confirmed in writing. My F BRE, A PAR, A MAR and F POR stay home this spring. In return, F NTH and A WAL stay off Biscay, MAO and the Channel, and no English unit approaches SPA or POR. Your A YOR should not drift toward Brest or Paris. Any breach ends our understanding. I have no plans against your centers in the north.

France to Germany, Spring 1947: My A PAR and A MAR will not enter Burgundy or the Ruhr this spring, and I will not support English attacks on your centers. Keep A MUN and A HOL out of Gascony, Marseille and Piedmont and we stay clear. England's fleets are the real danger to us both, so I will be watching them closely.

I’ll keep A BER, A HOL, A MUN and A NOR out of English centers this spring. I cannot concede KIE or DEN, but I’m not planning an attack on either this turn. Keep F NTH and F SKA away from German centers and do not support attacks on them; then we can avoid wasting units against each other.

Italy to France, Spring 1947: Agreed in principle. F TUN and F GOL will stay out of Spanish and Marseille waters this spring. I am watching Austria's A VEN closely since it sits in my home center and I will treat it as hostile unless it leaves. I am open to a Western Mediterranean understanding. Tell me if English fleets move toward Iberia or the Gulf of Lyon, and I will do the same.

Turkey to Austria, Spring 1947: My spring orders are not yet final. Your A SER and F GRE must stay out of BUL and CON, and your A BUD and A TRI must not enter RUM or SEV. I will keep A RUM, A SEV and A WAR off your home centers while that holds. Confirm your exact GRE and TRI orders first.

Turkey to England: I am focused on Austria's Balkan and Galician centers and have no plans toward the English north. Keep your fleets out of the Black Sea and eastern Mediterranean and we stay at peace.

Austria to Turkey, Fall 1947: Our units are now in contact and the old understanding is stale. Your A MOS, A SEV and A SMY are close to my southern and eastern holdings. Confirm in writing that none of your units will enter BUD, SER, TRI, VIE or GRE this fall, and I will keep A BUD, A SER and F GRE off BUL and CON. Tell me your exact orders for A BUL and A SEV.
